rules.description: Vi Mode: D as Trigger Key

rules.comment: This will disable Cmd + Shift + M in everye app unless you add the app id to the frontmost_application_unless block. Use `osascript -e 'id of app {APP_NAME}'` to determine the app name.

Workaround for a Colemak bug in the Claude app: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859. Note: the macOS Colemak input source re-translates Karabiner's output, so to send the app Cmd+K we emit key_code n (Colemak maps the n-position to 'k'). Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so Cmd+3 is emitted as-is.

Clicks the project selector on the New Conversation screen. Claude's Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the button cannot be targeted by name and the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display, so this only lands correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves, and the 100ms hold keeps the click from racing the cursor move.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+P -> click project selector (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Clicks the Create PR button in the session view. Like the Cmd+P project-selector rule, the Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display; y matches the project-selector rule, x is the button's position in a 2x Retina screenshot (1313 px) halved to points. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves. The 100ms hold is needed because without it the click races the cursor move and the app registers only the hover, so the shortcut had to be pressed twice.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+P -> click Create PR button (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Show Diff. The app ignores Cmd+Shift+D while the chat box has focus, so the rule first clicks an empty spot in the sidebar to blur it. Like the Cmd+P and Cmd+Shift+P rules, the coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves, since Karabiner runs shell_command asynchronously and would otherwise move the cursor first and leave the script saving (230, 940). Script startup measured 70-110ms over five runs, so 200ms is roughly twice the slowest; raise it if the cursor ever ends up parked in the sidebar. The two 100ms holds keep the click from racing the cursor move and give the app time to move focus before the keystroke arrives.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+G -> click empty sidebar (230, 940), Cmd+Shift+D

rules.comment: Same Colemak bug as the Cmd+J rule (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859): the app re-translates Karabiner's output through the macOS Colemak input source, so to send the app Cmd+Shift+U we emit key_code i (Colemak maps the i-position to 'u'). Period is not remapped by Colemak, so the from side is used as-is.
